# Recorded result schemas

These minimal JSON fixtures contain selected, unmodified result values from read-only primary-provider requests. Each fixture records its exact public source URL and retrieval time. No odds, predictions, credentials, names, season aggregate stats or research holdouts are included. They are result adapter fixtures, not a model evaluation dataset. NFL/NBA fields were verified on the authorized ESPN summary API; CFB has a separate result-only schema fixture for future genuine predictions. MLB uses the official Stats API live feed.

The NBA and football summary schema uses `header.id`, verified `header.league.id/uid` and matching event `header.uid`, exactly one `header.competitions` entry, two `homeAway` competitors, `status.type`, final scores and period `linescores.displayValue`. League UIDs are verified NFL `s:20~l:28`, NBA `s:40~l:46`, CFB `s:20~l:23`; mismatches cannot relabel a payload. Box scores use explicit athlete IDs and indexed `statistics.keys`/`athletes.stats`, never display labels or names. NBA explicit `didNotPlay` is distinct from an absent row. Positive recorded NBA minutes or football opportunities establish participation. Negative ESPN Team aggregate rows are not athlete IDs and are ignored. A player absent from a table is unknown, never a zero or a known nonparticipant.

MLB `gamePk` and `gameData.game.pk` must agree. Official team sport ID must be1 and `gameData.teams` home/away IDs must match boxscore teams. Only `liveData.boxscore.teams.*.players.ID<official-id>.stats` is used; `seasonStats` is never used. `gamesPlayed` establishes participation; an empty game stats object stays unknown. MLB `metaData.timeStamp` supplies provider revision/update time. ESPN summary contains no verified result update timestamp, so `sourceUpdatedAt` and `providerRevision` remain null. `retrievedAt` is independent retrieval metadata.

Canonical provider identities are `mlb:<id>` and `espn:<lowercase-sport>:<id>`. Predictions must supply the same canonical event/player identities and exact `sourceIds.provider/event/player`. Other providers need a separately authoritative exact-ID crosswalk before capture/settlement; these adapters never resolve names, dates or matchup abbreviations. New sport result adapters are unavailable and return UNKNOWN; scoped NHL/tennis/soccer predictions stay UNRESOLVED.

`sourceRevision` is the stable, sorted JSON serialization of all normalized result facts, including source, sport, provider IDs, status, periods, player facts and provider update/revision. It excludes retrieval time. This exact content identity detects corrected scores/stats even when ESPN does not expose an update timestamp and avoids hash collisions. It is an identity, not a sortable timestamp or a numeric database revision. A settlement worker should compare it with the last stored settlement payload, append on a change, allocate `revision`/`supersedesRevision` transactionally and supply `settledAt`. The pure grader leaves those worker-owned fields null. The existing append settlement RPC retains the full payload, so no schema extension is required for this identity.

Saved rules must explicitly contain `version`, exact `book` matching the prediction, `period`, `tie`, `cancelled`, `shortened`, `nonparticipant` and `appearance`. These are a conservative grading contract, not asserted bookmaker rules. The fixture policy is synthetic (`fixture-book`) and must never be assigned to production observations as a default. Supported periods: MLB FULL_GAME; NFL/NBA/CFB REGULATION or INCLUDING_OVERTIME. Supported tokens: tie PUSH/VOID/UNRESOLVED (moneyline), cancelled VOID/UNRESOLVED, shortened VOID/UNRESOLVED/ACTION (ACTION additionally requires positive integer `minimumPeriods`), nonparticipant VOID/UNRESOLVED, appearance ANY_APPEARANCE. MLB minimum periods means whole completed innings proven by `currentInning`/`inningState`/`outs`, never a rounded-up reached inning. Fractional innings and starter/plate-appearance bookmaker policies need separate tested contracts and remain unsupported here. Unknown or missing tokens stay unresolved. Regulation props are unavailable when overtime is true/unknown because summary boxscores contain whole-game stats.

Supported stats are exported as `RESULT_STATS` and tested with recorded values. MLB `pitching_strikeouts` is the explicit existing observation stat ID mapped to official `strikeOuts`; `pitching_strikeOuts` is also an explicit provider-field spelling. Basketball composite markets require every constituent count. Missing/null/malformed counts remain null. Cancellation, postponement, correction, tie, shortened final and overtime cases in tests are explicit mutations of recorded provider facts or normalized facts; they do not claim a live cancelled/tied/shortened fixture.

No result fetcher, settlement scheduler or production deployment is implemented in this task. Upstream HTTP failures belong to the authenticated worker, must remain unresolved and must not be normalized as an empty success.
